content.comment_body: Hello, I have updated my [product_name] programming software to [version_no] and I'm working with a [product_name] device, firmware version [version_no]. When I attempt to run an online test, I receive an error stating: "Online test failed. The hardware type of the programming software does not match the connected device." I have confirmed that my hardware type displays as [version_no]. However, I noticed that online testing works flawlessly with previous versions like [version_no]. My questions are: Is there a firmware upgrade available for my [product_name]? Given my device type [article_no], can it support all the new features in the latest programming software, or is purchasing a new [product_name] necessary? Best regards, [user_name]

It is not possible to upgrade a [product_name] with [version_no] firmware to a newer version like [version_no]. No firmware update exists for this purpose. To utilize the new features provided in the latest software release, a new [product_name] with [version_no] is required.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encounter incompatibility between newer programming software versions and legacy hardware, causing failed online testing and missing features. The central issue is that new software capabilities are not available to older devices due to hardware limitations and the lack of firmware upgrade options.
analysis.user_expectations: Users desire either backward compatibility or the ability to upgrade older hardware to access enhanced features in updated programming software, particularly for online testing. They seek clarification regarding firmware upgrades and guidance on whether obtaining new hardware is necessary.
